title: Design System: ASM Gate & Door Services

display.purpose: Inner-page hero headings and the closing call-to-action band; width 125, capped at 6rem.

headline-lg.purpose: h1 outside heroes and the residential/commercial panel headings.

headline.purpose: Every section heading (h2) and catalogue category titles; width 118.

title.purpose: h3: pillar and value titles, rail card names, the quote form heading.

title-sm.purpose: h4: FAQ questions, project and process step titles.

lead.purpose: One-paragraph intro under a heading, in the soft foreground, 40 to 52ch.

body.purpose: Reading text at width 100; prose capped at 68ch.

label.purpose: Data and field labels, sentence case, 0.01em tracking. Never a kicker above a heading.

control.purpose: Buttons, link-arrows, header CTA, mobile action bar: the only uppercase tracked type.

shadows.name: groove-light
shadows.purpose: The 2px seam where light bands meet and where ruled lists open on light grounds (dark line over light line).

shadows.name: groove-dark
shadows.purpose: The 2px seam on dark bands, under the header and above the footer.

shadows.name: overlay-drop
shadows.purpose: Only for the services mega menu, which floats over the page.

shadows.name: selected-edge
shadows.purpose: Bronze bar on the left edge of a selected service tile.

shadows.name: error-edge
shadows.purpose: Signal Red bar on the left edge of an invalid field.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Text fields on focus, with the border turning Ink.

shadows.name: door-seal
shadows.purpose: The bottom seal of the hero door stack; signature-only.

shadows.name: door-panel-bevel
shadows.purpose: Top highlight and bottom shadow on each hero door panel; signature-only.

shadows.name: hero-scrim
shadows.purpose: Ironsand scrim that keeps bottom-left hero type legible over photography.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Expo-like default for state changes, arrow nudges, image settles and entrances.

motion.name: ease-door
motion.purpose: Door easing: hero door lift, image clip wipes, mobile menu wipe.

motion.name: t-fast
motion.purpose: Colour, border and background changes on hover.

motion.name: t-med
motion.purpose: Arrow nudges, underline growth, header state, action bar slide.

motion.name: door-lift
motion.purpose: Home hero signature: six charcoal panels lift off the photograph on load. Not rendered under reduced motion.

motion.name: reveal-wipe
motion.value: clip-path inset(100% 0 0 0) to inset(0) (bottom-up), 1.1s ease-door; img scale 1.06 to 1, 1.6s ease-out
motion.purpose: Photo frames with data-reveal open as they enter the viewport; only with JS and motion allowed.

motion.name: hero-rise
motion.purpose: Hero copy settles into place; never starts invisible.

motion.name: image-hover-zoom
motion.purpose: Photo inside a frame on card hover.

narrative.overview:
Every page is built the way a sectional garage door is built: a stack of full-width horizontal panels in two materials, ironsand steel and pale limestone, joined at machined groove lines, with anodised bronze as the only hardware. The visitor reads the site top to bottom the way they would read a door: panel, seam, panel. Photography fills panels edge to edge or sits in hard-edged frames; type is cut from one variable family whose width axis does the work a second typeface would normally do.

The mood is architectural, industrial and quietly premium: heavy expanded display type over dark photographs, generous section padding, long ruled lists instead of card grids, and a single warm metal accent that only ever appears where something can be pressed, is active, or is a small piece of hardware. Density is low on marketing bands and higher in the catalogue and quote form, where ruled rows and spec tables carry the detail.

Motion borrows from the door itself. On the home page a stack of charcoal panels lifts off the hero photograph on load; across the site, photographs open with a vertical clip wipe as they enter the viewport. Both disappear under reduced motion, and text is never hidden waiting for an animation. The system rejects the generic trade-site look the brief ruled out: template layouts, excessive gradients, cartoon illustration, rounded card grids, colourful layouts and decorative animation.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials only: ironsand darks and limestone/bone lights, alternating band by band.
One accent: anodised bronze, for actions, active states, rules and small hardware (icons).
Bands meet at a 2px groove seam (dark line over light line), like the joint between two door panels.
Archivo Variable throughout; expanded width (118 to 125) and heavy weight for headings, normal width for reading.
Square geometry: 2px radius on controls, 0 on frames and panels.
Ruled rows and hairlines instead of boxed, shadowed cards.
Door-like motion: hero door lift and vertical image wipes, all off under reduced motion.
Honest by construction: unconfirmed facts carry a dotted underline; stock photos carry a "Representative image" tag.

rules.name: The One Hardware Rule
rules.body: Bronze is the only accent, and it appears only on actions, active and selected states, 2px rules and indicators, and small hardware details such as icons. It is never a band ground, a card fill, a heading colour, or a decorative wash.

rules.name: The Two Materials Rule
rules.body: Every surface is ironsand or limestone/bone. A band declares its material with a context (dark, light or bone), which remaps foreground, soft text, line, strong line, accent text and surface together; components read those semantic roles and never hard-code a material.

rules.name: The Bronze-by-Context Rule
rules.body: Bronze fills carry Ironsand text, never white. Bronze as text uses Bronze Ink on light grounds and Bronze Glint on dark grounds, so it always clears AA.

rules.name: The Width-Is-Rank Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is set by width as much as size: 125 for display, 118 for headings, 106 to 112 for labels and controls, 100 for anything read in sentences. Reading text is never expanded.

rules.name: The Controls-Only Caps Rule
rules.body: Uppercase with 0.08em tracking belongs to controls alone. Labels are sentence case at 0.01em, and no kicker or eyebrow line ever sits above a heading: the heading opens the band.

rules.name: The Groove Seam Rule
rules.body: Every band of a page meets the next at a 2px groove, a dark 1px line over a light 1px line (light groove on light bands, dark groove on dark bands and the footer). The major ruled lists inside a band open on the same groove. Bands never meet at a gap, a hard border, or a fade.

rules.name: The Alternating Ground Rule
rules.body: Adjacent bands never share a ground: dark, limestone and bone take turns down the page. Forms always sit on a light ground, even inside a dark band.

rules.name: The Ruled Row Rule
rules.body: Repeated items (services, pillars, process steps, FAQs, symptoms, service areas, controls) are ruled rows separated by 1px hairlines in the band's line or strong-line colour, not boxed cards in a grid.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit flat. A shadow appears only when something floats over the page (the mega menu) or marks state (selected, invalid, focused); resting cards and sections never cast one.

rules.name: The Square Edge Rule
rules.body: Nothing exceeds a 2px radius. No pills, no rounded cards, no circular avatars or icon badges.

rules.name: The Visible Placeholder Rule
rules.body: Anything the business has not confirmed is shown with the dotted placeholder underline until real content replaces it; it is never styled to look final.

rules.name: The Provenance Tag Rule
rules.body: Every stock photograph that can be read as ASM's own work carries the "Representative image" tag.

rules.name: The Door Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion moves like a door: vertical lifts and vertical clip wipes on the door easing (cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.18, 1)), small state changes on the expo-out easing at 160 to 320ms. Every animation is off under reduced motion, and no text waits on one to appear.

dos: Do build every page as a stack of full-width bands that alternate between ironsand, limestone and bone, each joined to the next by the 2px groove seam.
Do keep bronze for actions, active and selected states, 2px rules and indicators, and small hardware such as icons; use Bronze Ink for bronze text on light and Bronze Glint on dark.
Do set headings in Archivo Variable at width 118 to 125 and weight 700 to 800 with tight negative tracking, and reading text at width 100, weight 400, 1.6 line height.
Do set data and field labels in sentence case (0.8125rem, weight 620, 0.01em tracking).
Do present repeated items as ruled rows with 1px hairlines, opening on a groove.
Do frame photography edge to edge or in square frames at fixed ratios, with an Ironsand scrim wherever type sits on an image.
Do mark unconfirmed facts with the dotted placeholder underline and tag stock photos "Representative image".
Do keep a quote action and a call action within reach on every page and every phone screen.
Do give every animation a reduced-motion fallback and keep text visible from the first frame.
donts: Don't put kicker or eyebrow text above a heading.
Don't use uppercase tracked lettering outside controls (buttons, link-arrows, the header CTA, the mobile action bar).
Don't use bronze as a band ground, card fill, heading colour or decorative wash, and don't put white text on a bronze fill.
Don't introduce a second accent colour or a third ground material.
Don't round anything beyond 2px or use pills, rounded cards or circular badges.
Don't box repeated items in shadowed cards or lay them out as a row of equal icon cards.
Don't separate bands with gaps, hard borders or fades instead of the groove seam.
Don't use gradients as fills; gradients exist only as photo scrims, the groove itself and the hero door's panel shading.
Don't expand the width axis of reading text.
Don't mix icon families or use glyph icons; use the single 1.6-stroke, square-cap set.
